basics.name: Amir Ali Jiwani
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer — Pascal & .NET
basics.summary: Senior engineer with strong foundations in Pascal and extensive C#/.NET experience across CLI, desktop, web and device-integration projects. Experienced in low-level programming (structs, pointers, IO), compiler concepts, COM interop, IIS/ASP.NET and modern .NET Core / Azure deployments. Comfortable translating legacy Pascal systems to maintainable C# codebases and delivering robust device-control and enterprise integration solutions.

work.position: Founder / CTO — Device integrations & Desktop apps
work.summary: Led cross-platform desktop and device-integrated projects; built reusable frameworks and native integrations using Pascal and C#.
highlights: Developed multiple management systems and CLI tools in Pascal during university and early product development, using structs, pointers and low-level IO for device control.
Built desktop apps and device-control integrations using C# with COM interop to call low-level device APIs and orchestrate hardware workflows.
Authored reusable libraries and frameworks (games and utilities) to accelerate development across desktop and embedded integrations.

work.summary: Worked on .NET Core proof-of-concepts and cloud-native deployments while maintaining legacy ASP.NET/IIS services; introduced modern API patterns and Kestrel-based hosting.
highlights: Led migration experiments from legacy ASP.NET/IIS to .NET Core APIs hosted on Kestrel and Azure, demonstrating performance and deployment benefits.
Implemented web APIs and integration points (SOAP/WCF and new RESTful services) to bridge legacy customers and modern clients.
Built developer tooling and CI/CD pipelines to support repeatable deployment and testing of .NET services.

work.summary: Academic and personal projects using Pascal including a mini Pascal compiler and multiple management/CLI systems interfacing with hardware.
highlights: Implemented a mini Pascal compiler as part of Compiler Construction coursework — lexical analysis, parsing, symbol tables and basic code generation.
Built CLI tools with animated console output and complex problem-solving routines for data processing in Pascal.
Implemented hardware IO control code (reading/writing ports, signal handling) for embedded/desktop device projects using Pascal and later interfacing via C#.

work.summary: Worked across SOAP, Silverlight, ASP.NET and desktop apps; deployed and managed IIS-hosted services and desktop integrations.
highlights: Built and maintained ASP.NET web apps and SOAP integrations for clients, including IIS deployment and configuration.
Developed Silverlight/UIs and desktop tooling for internal workflows; used COM interop for device management where required.
Ported and documented legacy Pascal modules into C# proofs-of-concept to validate maintainability and integration approaches.

projects.name: Pascal mini-compiler
projects.description: Academic project implementing lexer, parser, symbol table and simple code generation for a subset of Pascal. Demonstrated compiler construction concepts and language runtime behaviour.

projects.name: Device control via COM interop (C#)
projects.description: Integrated and orchestrated low-level device signals using COM objects and portable C# wrappers to provide deterministic control flows across desktop and embedded clients.

projects.name: Legacy Pascal → C# migration POCs
projects.description: Translated Pascal-based management modules into C# prototypes, demonstrating clearer API boundaries, test coverage and maintainability improvements for client adoption.

meta.notes: Tailored for roles requiring Pascal and .NET expertise. Emphasises low-level programming, compiler and device integration experience plus legacy-to-modern .NET migration capability.
